attribution.note: Marcus's own prediction in his 1 January 2025 post, listed under 'High confidence'. These are his words, not a quote of someone else.

semantics.note: An unqualified 'will' under 'High confidence' makes this a scored forecast. 'Possibly' only qualifies the narrow-use exception, not the main claim. The normalised wording keeps the 2025 horizon, both parts (hype and unreliability) and the exception.

contract.note: Reading 'far from reliable' as high failure rates on realistic multi-step tasks is the evaluator's choice, not the speaker's metric. Still, any reasonable reading gives the same result when the best agents complete 2.5–30% of tasks. Excluding narrow uses respects the speaker's exception.

evidence.note: January 2025 post by OpenAI's CEO saying agents may 'join the workforce'. It shows agents being promoted at the start of the year. It is a company statement, used only as evidence of hype, not of reliability.
June 2025 post by OpenAI's CEO saying agents doing 'real cognitive work' had arrived. It shows promotion continuing mid-year. It is a company claim, not a test; its coding example is a narrower use.

Independent benchmark preprint, revised September 2025. The best agent completed only 30% of simulated workplace tasks, and long-horizon tasks were out of reach, so most realistic multi-step work tasks failed.
OpenAI launched AgentKit on 6 October 2025, showing agents still promoted in the last quarter. Klarna's support agent is a narrow use case, which the speaker excepted.
Independent preprint from 30 October 2025 on real paid projects across many sectors. The best agent automated 2.5% of them, which meets the contract's test for late 2025.

output.rationale: The 2025 horizon has passed. Leading companies promoted agents in January, June and October 2025, including the last quarter. Independent tests from September and October 2025 found the best general-purpose agents completing 30% and 2.5% of realistic work tasks. Possible counterexamples (Klarna support, coding) are narrow uses the speaker excepted. No December test is in the record, but the late-October test meets the contract's 'late 2025' requirement.
